boards.title: Your First Weekend at Elmhurst University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A ten-stop, under-21-safe sequence for learning the campus, finding student spaces, and exploring nearby public destinations from Friday through Sunday.

cards.title: 1. Start at the Gates of Knowledge
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · 190 Prospect Avenue
cards.notes: Enter through the official campus gateway, take an orientation photo, and use the arch as your reference point for the weekend.
cards.short_summary: Begin at Elmhurst University’s named official entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University identifies the Gates of Knowledge at 190 Prospect Avenue as its official entrance.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies this as the University’s official entrance; no building access is required to view the gate.

cards.title: 2. Learn Campus Through Its Trees
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Across the 48-acre campus
cards.notes: Open the interactive arboretum map and trace a short loop through campus, noting plant labels and landmarks for later navigation.
cards.short_summary: Use the campus-wide living collection as an outdoor orientation route.
cards.evidence_claim: The Elmhurst University Arboretum encompasses the entire 48-acre campus, and the University welcomes visitors throughout the year.
cards.access_notes: The University welcomes visitors throughout the year and links an interactive map for planning a tour.

cards.title: 3. Find the Student Hangout
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Frick Center
cards.notes: Locate the Roost, Game Room, and nearby Information Desk so you know where to pause, ask questions, or meet classmates later.
cards.short_summary: Map the Frick Center’s principal student gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Office of Student Involvement oversees the Frick Center’s Information Desk, Game Room, and Bluejays’ Roost.
cards.source_title: Office of Student Involvement & Frick Center
cards.access_notes: This is a campus student space; follow posted Frick Center access and operating information.

cards.title: 4. Scout a Future Study Room
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Upper and lower levels
cards.notes: Walk through both study-room areas and identify one group room upstairs and one single room downstairs for your first busy week.
cards.short_summary: Preview the library’s group and individual study options.
cards.evidence_claim: A.C. Buehler Library offers reservable group study rooms on its upper level and single study rooms on its lower level.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms are for students and can be reserved; consult the library’s current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: 5. Add a Public Study Backup
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 125 South Prospect Avenue
cards.notes: Save the address and contact details, then browse the building before its posted Friday closing time so you have an off-campus option.
cards.short_summary: Establish a nearby public-library fallback for evening work.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst Public Library is at 125 South Prospect Avenue and lists Monday–Friday hours of 9:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Friday hours are currently listed as 9:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.; check the homepage for holiday or special closures.

cards.title: 6. Take a Saturday Park Loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · 175 South Prospect Avenue
cards.notes: Follow the walking paths past the gardens and cultural buildings, noting picnic areas, restrooms, and the route back toward campus.
cards.short_summary: Orient yourself to Elmhurst’s nearby civic and cultural hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Wilder Park contains walking paths, a running trail, picnic areas, restrooms, gardens, and several cultural facilities.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park access is subject to Elmhurst Park District rules, weather conditions, and any posted closures.

cards.title: 7. Step Inside the Conservatory
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · 225 South Prospect Avenue
cards.notes: Walk through the greenhouse displays, leave food outside, avoid feeding the fish, and keep casual photography clear of posed sessions.
cards.short_summary: Pause among the conservatory’s year-round horticultural displays.
cards.evidence_claim: Wilder Park Conservatory is free and open to the public year-round, with April–December hours listed as 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: April–December hours are 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. daily; check for weather, maintenance, or flower-show installation closures.

cards.title: 8. Choose an Art-Museum Session
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · 150 South Cottage Hill Avenue
cards.notes: Bring a student ID for the listed student rate and budget time for the galleries, McCormick House, and Elmhurst Artists’ Guild.
cards.short_summary: Add a ticketed visual-arts stop beside Wilder Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst Art Museum is open Friday–Sunday from 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; student admission with school ID is listed as $10.
cards.access_notes: Saturday hours are currently 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; federal-holiday closures apply, and admission is required.

cards.title: 9. Put the Town in Context
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · 120 East Park Avenue
cards.notes: Browse the local-history exhibits, then mark the nearby Metra station and downtown landmarks before walking back toward campus.
cards.short_summary: Learn how Elmhurst developed through a city-operated museum.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst History Museum is operated by the City of Elmhurst, offers free general admission, and is open Saturdays from 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Saturday hours are 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; general admission is free, while tours and select programs may charge fees.

cards.title: 10. Finish by Planning a Workout
cards.subtitle: Sunday reset · Faganel Hall
cards.notes: Save the front-desk number, inspect the posted schedule, and pack your Jaypass for a weekday return when the center is confirmed open.
cards.short_summary: Close the weekend by locating the student fitness facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Tyrrell Fitness Center contains strength and cardiovascular workout areas and requires a current Jaypass for entry.
cards.access_notes: The posted summer schedule says weekends are closed; current students need a Jaypass, guests are not allowed, and calling ahead is recommended.
